summary: Arabic compares with one special form of the adjective, the elative أَفْعَلُ (ʾafʿal, “more / most”): كَبِير → أَكْبَرُ, صَغِير → أَصْغَرُ, جَمِيل → أَجْمَلُ, سَرِيع → أَسْرَعُ. With مِنْ it is the comparative: الْبَيْتُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الشَّقَّةِ (the house is bigger than the flat) — “than” is the same مِنْ as “from”, as in Greek μεγαλύτερος από. With the article, or before a noun in the genitive, it is the superlative: الْبَيْتُ الْأَكْبَرُ (the biggest house), أَكْبَرُ بَيْتٍ فِي الْقَرْيَةِ (the biggest house in the village). The comparative does not change for gender or number — أَخِي أَكْبَرُ مِنِّي, أُخْتِي أَكْبَرُ مِنِّي — and it is a diptote: أَكْبَرُ, accusative and genitive أَكْبَرَ, never with tanwīn. Roots with a doubled or weak letter keep their shape: حَارّ → أَحَرُّ, قَرِيب → أَقْرَبُ, بَطِيء → أَبْطَأُ, سَيِّئ → أَسْوَأُ (worse), غَالٍ → أَغْلَى (never changes). “Better” is أَفْضَلُ (or أَحْسَنُ), not a form of جَيِّد. Adjectives that cannot take the pattern — the colours, participles like مُتْعَب — use أَكْثَرُ (more) or أَشَدُّ + a noun in the accusative: أَكْثَرُ تَعَبًا (more tired), أَكْثَرُ حُمْرَةً (redder). أَكْثَرُ is itself the elative of كَثِير: “more” (أُحِبُّ الشَّايَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ الْقَهْوَةِ) and, before a definite plural, “most of” (أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ). The colours have a pattern of their own that looks like the elative: أَحْمَرُ (m.), حَمْرَاءُ (f.), حُمْرٌ (pl.) — with no tanwīn in the singular; the newer colour words in -iyy (بُنِّيّ, رَمَادِيّ, بُرْتُقَالِيّ, وَرْدِيّ, بَنَفْسَجِيّ) are regular. Light and dark shades follow the colour: أَزْرَقُ فَاتِحٌ, أَخْضَرُ غَامِقٌ.

blocks.title: The comparative does not agree.
blocks.text: الطَّائِرَةُ أَسْرَعُ مِنَ الْقِطَارِ (the plane, f., is faster than the train) — أُخْتِي أَكْبَرُ مِنِّي. Only the superlative with al- may take a feminine form: الْكُبْرَى, الصُّغْرَى (أُخْتِي الصُّغْرَى, my youngest sister).

blocks.title: No tanwīn on the elative.
blocks.text: أَكْبَرُ, not *أَكْبَرٌ; after لَيْسَ or a verb it is أَكْبَرَ: أَخِي لَيْسَ أَطْوَلَ مِنِّي, أُحِبُّ الشَّايَ أَكْثَرَ.

blocks.title: Light and dark.
blocks.text: فَاتِح (light) and غَامِق (dark) follow the colour: أَزْرَقُ فَاتِحٌ, أَخْضَرُ غَامِقٌ. With a feminine noun the safe way is to name the colour (لَوْن, m.): لَوْنُ السَّيَّارَةِ أَزْرَقُ غَامِقٌ. A dark room is مُظْلِمَة, not غَامِقَة.

blocks.title: A red car, red cars.
blocks.text: سَيَّارَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ — and things in the plural are feminine singular: سَيَّارَاتٌ حَمْرَاءُ, هٰذِهِ أَقْلَامٌ حَمْرَاءُ.
“Than me, than you”: مِنْ takes its pronoun endings (lesson 11): أَخِي أَكْبَرُ مِنِّي, أَنْتَ أَطْوَلُ مِنْهُ. “More than” with a verb: يَأْكُلُ أَخِي أَكْثَرَ مِنِّي.

askYourself: Am I comparing two things? → elative + مِنْ (genitive after مِنْ; a pronoun: مِنِّي, مِنْكَ).
Is it the highest degree? → الْـ + elative after the noun, or the elative + an indefinite noun in the genitive (أَكْبَرُ بَيْتٍ).
Does this adjective have an elative? Colours, participles, -ān adjectives don’t → أَكْثَرُ / أَشَدُّ + a noun in the accusative.
Is the noun feminine or plural? → the comparative stays the same (أَكْبَرُ).
Does it stand after a verb or after لَيْسَ / كَانَ? → accusative أَكْبَرَ (no tanwīn).
A colour: masculine or feminine noun? → أَحْمَرُ / حَمْرَاءُ; things in the plural → حَمْرَاءُ.

traps: *أَكْبَرٌ → أَكْبَرُ: the elative is a diptote.
*الطَّائِرَةُ سُرْعَى مِنَ الْقِطَارِ → الطَّائِرَةُ أَسْرَعُ مِنَ الْقِطَارِ: the comparative does not agree.
“Better” is أَفْضَلُ / أَحْسَنُ, not a form of جَيِّد.

quiz.why: The comparative does not change for a woman.
Elative + an indefinite noun in the genitive = the -est.
The feminine of أَحْمَر is حَمْرَاء.
أَغْلَى never changes; after مِنْ the genitive.
فَاتِح follows the colour; غَامِق is dark.
أَكْثَرُ + a definite plural = most of; أَكْثَرُ مِنَ النَّاسِ is “more than the people”.

seeAlso.note: Hebrew has no special form: יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל מִ… (more big than), הֲכִי גָּדוֹל (the biggest); its “than” is מִ / מֵאֲשֶׁר — the same מִן as Arabic مِنْ.
German: größer als, am größten / der größte — endings; Arabic changes the whole pattern of the word (كَبِير → أَكْبَر), and its “than” is “from” (مِنْ) where German has als.
Chinese leaves the adjective alone: A 比 B 大 (A is bigger than B), 最大 (the biggest), 更 (even more).
The positive forms and their agreement (lesson 16); the comparative is the one adjective form that does not agree.
مِنْ with pronoun endings — مِنِّي, مِنْكَ, مِنْهُ — is “than me, than you, than him”.
